messages:
cassie: heads-up — eu-west2 just had a big noisy event: ephemeral-cleaner kicked off and IOPS shot ~3-4x during the nightly window. GPU attaches started failing within the 15m window. logs attached below and a quick correlate with GPU queue waits.

infra-bot: alert: high-disk-io on nvme-ephemeral-pool-eu-west2 (avg r/s+w/s spike) :warning:

cassie: short dump from the host (iostat):
```
Device            r/s    w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await   r_await w_await  %util
nvme0n1         120.5  310.2  15360   49280    170.0    12.3      8.5     2.3     9.1    95.6
nvme1n1           98.1  210.7  12480   33440    178.2    9.1      6.9     1.8     7.2    86.2
```

cassie: overlayfs scrub was running with cleaner concurrency at 8. Looks like a change in the janitor canary yesterday bumped concurrency and removed a backoff.

kevin: ugh — that explains the attach stalls. We hit the same pattern when scrub concurrency was increased in ap-south last month.

maria: can we throttle the cleaner at the daemon level? quick patch to set concurrency=2 and enable adaptive-backoff should help.

alex: +1 to reducing concurrency. Quick mitigation: patch the fleet configmap for the cleaner to set `MAX_CONCURRENCY=2` and `SLEEP_BASE_MS=200` then roll in a small canary to eu-west2-az-a.

cassie: trying that now on one canary host. will post results in ~10m.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: configmap updated: ephemeral-cleaner-config -> rollout started (canary eu-west2-az-a) :rocket:

cassie: canary looks good — iops down ~55% on that host, gpu attach succeeded for 12/12 jobs in the last 8m.

tamika: timeline note: this spike caused ~6 failed gpu attaches across prod (15m) and a ~2% increase in on-demand fallback cost. we should capture cost hit for the incident log.

kevin: next steps:
- keep canary for 30m
- if stable, roll to 20% of eu-west2 then full region
- create a regression test that simulates overlayfs scrub + heavy kv-cache warmups to catch this earlier

maria: also file an ops-change to revert that prior canary that removed adaptive backoff. I'll draft the revert PR.

alex: FYI command I ran on the canary node: `kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/ephemeral-cleaner MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 SLEEP_BASE_MS=200 --record`

cassie: putting a short-term rule in the scheduler: prefer nodes with io_util < 60% for gpu attach until rollout done. just made a quick filter in the attach controller.

tamika: good call. tagging oncall for postmortem: @kevin @cassie @maria. please capture: root cause (removed backoff), timeline, mitigations, and cost impact.

kevin: can someone paste the PR/commit that bumped concurrency? want it in the postmortem.

cassie: found it — `infra/ops: cleaner: remove-adaptive-backoff` commit 6c3b9e4. adding to the doc.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout completed to 20% (eu-west2) — monitoring.

maria: when we do full rollout, add an autoscaler knob: if avg_qu_sz > 8 then force concurrency down to 1. defensive guard.

cassie: agreed. also scheduling a small soak-run (2h) running our kv-cache warmup script to validate before full region roll.

tamika: thanks all. I'll open the incident ticket and include the cost delta estimate (2% on-demand bump).

kevin: reminder: add a post-deploy test to CI that runs a synthetic cleaner + attach flow so we don't regress this silently.

maria: noted. will add test and the autoscaler guard in the same PR.

cassie: resolved for now — will update thread after full roll. :white_check_mark:
